bugs.error_message: PostToolUse:write hook error — Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '/workspaces/gustik/.wolf/hooks/symbol-extractor.js' imported from /workspaces/gustik/.wolf/hooks/post-write.js
bugs.root_cause: The OpenWolf install commit (f532148, 'chore: add OpenWolf files and CLAUDE.md') never copied symbol-extractor.js into .wolf/hooks/, even though post-write.js imports it. Every other hook file was present and matched the version shipped in the globally installed openwolf@2.0.1 npm package (dist/hooks/*.js), so this was an install/packaging gap, not a version mismatch. Because post-write.js's main() wraps everything in main().catch(() => process.exit(0)), runtime errors inside main are swallowed silently — but a top-level ESM import failure happens before main() is ever called, so it crashed loudly on every Write/Edit/MultiEdit for the whole session instead of being masked like other errors would be.
bugs.fix: Copied .wolf/hooks/symbol-extractor.js from /usr/lib/node_modules/openwolf/dist/hooks/symbol-extractor.js (globally installed openwolf@2.0.1 — confirmed same version via diff against the project's post-write.js, which matched byte-for-byte except a sourceMappingURL comment). Verified by piping a synthetic Write tool_input JSON into `node .wolf/hooks/post-write.js` and confirming exit code 0. Ran `openwolf scan` afterward to backfill anatomy.md entries that the hook had failed to write during the outage. File is untracked in git as of this fix — needs `git add .wolf/hooks/symbol-extractor.js` to persist.

bugs.error_message: Stop hook repeats 'ACTION REQUIRED: N files were modified this session but no semantic summary was written to memory.md' every single turn, even after a proper semantic summary line is appended.
bugs.root_cause: countSemanticEntries() (shared.js:614-631) requires a memory.md line to start with `| ${today}` where today is a full ISO date like '| 2026-08-01'. But every memory.md row actually written by post-write.js/stop.js is time-only, formatted `| HH:MM | ... |` (the date only appears once, in the '## Session: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' heading above each table). Since no row line ever starts with the date, the startsWith(todayPrefix) check never matches, semanticCount is always 0, and needsSemanticSummary() (stop.js:206-213) fires unconditionally on every Stop regardless of how many real summaries exist — an unsatisfiable check.
bugs.fix: Patched countSemanticEntries() in .wolf/hooks/shared.js: instead of matching row lines against an impossible `| ${today}` date prefix, it now tracks which '## Session: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' heading block it's inside and counts non-mechanical `| HH:MM | ... |` rows within today's session block(s). Verified via `node -e "import('./.wolf/hooks/shared.js').then(({countSemanticEntries,getWolfDir}) => console.log(countSemanticEntries(getWolfDir())))"` — now correctly returns 2 instead of 0.

bugs.error_message: Stop hook: 'Files edited 3+ times this session (ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md) but buglog.json was not updated.' — false-positive trigger, not an actual bug.
bugs.root_cause: Not a bug — the multi-edit heuristic can't distinguish 'fixing a mistake repeatedly' from a document going through a defined multi-pass authoring process. ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md was edited 6+ times in one session because the bmad-architecture skill's Finalize sequence is inherently multi-pass by design: Fast-path draft, then a 3-lens reviewer gate (rubric checklist + version/currency + adversarial-divergence, each a parallel subagent) whose findings get applied back into the same file as separate, scoped edits (one per AD/section fixed).
bugs.fix: No code fix needed. Logging this so a future session reading buglog.json before re-debugging doesn't mistake repeated edits to a BMAD spine/PRD/spec artifact for a sign something went wrong — that pattern is expected for any bmad-* skill with a reviewer-gate Finalize step, not just this run.

bugs.error_message: Stop hook kept repeating 'ACTION REQUIRED: Files edited 3+ times this session ... but buglog.json was not updated' every turn, even immediately after bug-003 was logged to buglog.json in the previous turn.
bugs.root_cause: checkForMissingBugLogs() (stop.js:145-158) checked `session.files_written.some(w => w.file.includes("buglog.json"))` to decide whether buglog.json had been updated. But post-write.js exits early for every path under .wolf/ ('Skip processing for .wolf/ internal files to avoid slow self-referential updates', post-write.js:39-42) — before it ever reaches the line that pushes to session.files_written. So writes to .wolf/buglog.json itself can never appear in files_written, and the check was unsatisfiable: no edit to buglog.json, however correct or recent, could ever clear the reminder. Same bug *class* as bug-002 (a Stop-hook check whose required evidence structurally can never be produced), but an independent root cause/code path — that one was a date-format mismatch in shared.js, this one is a tracking-array exclusion colliding with a check that assumed inclusion.
bugs.fix: Rewrote checkForMissingBugLogs() to check buglog.json's own mtime via fs.statSync against session.started, mirroring the pattern checkStatusFreshness() already used correctly for STATUS.md (which checks the file's mtime directly, not files_written). Verified by replicating the exact comparison inline against the real buglog.json mtime and the current session's recorded `started` timestamp — now correctly evaluates true after an edit, where it was unconditionally false before.

bugs.error_message: 500 Internal Server Error: 'socket.send is not a function' on GET /readings/live (WS route); WS client connection fails / hangs
bugs.root_cause: @fastify/websocket (v11.0.2) attaches its route-interception (onRoute) hook asynchronously during its own plugin registration. Calling `fastify.register(fastifyWebsocket)` without awaiting it, then declaring `{websocket:true}` routes synchronously in the very next statement on the SAME fastify instance, runs the route registration before the hook is live - the route is treated as a plain HTTP route and the handler receives something that is not a real ws.WebSocket (no .send method), even though app.listen()/app.inject() eventually resolves the plugin boot queue fine for everything else.
bugs.fix: Declare all `{websocket:true}` (and any) routes inside a nested `fastify.register(async (instance) => { ...routes... })` child plugin context registered AFTER `fastify.register(fastifyWebsocket)`, matching the pattern in the @fastify/websocket README. Avvio (Fastify's plugin boot system) guarantees a child .register() call is fully sequenced after the parent plugin it follows, which a bare synchronous route declaration in the same context is not.

bugs.error_message: undefined reference to pulsesToWindSpeedMs(...) at link time under `pio test -e native`, despite src/correct/wind_speed.cpp existing and platformio.ini's build_src_filter listing it
bugs.root_cause: PlatformIO's unit test runner does NOT compile src/ into the test build by default, regardless of build_src_filter - that filter only controls the app build. Needed the separate `test_build_src = yes` option to pull src/ (filtered) into the test binary too. A second, unrelated issue stacked on top: PlatformIO's bundled Unity is built WITHOUT double-precision assertion support by default (`UNITY_INCLUDE_DOUBLE` undefined), so TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_DOUBLE silently reports 'Unity Double Precision Disabled' failures even once linking succeeded.
bugs.fix: In the [env:native] section: add `test_build_src = yes`, and add `build_flags = -DUNITY_INCLUDE_DOUBLE`. Both are required for any native-test env testing double-returning pure logic (wind speed, yaw correction, etc.) - carry them into every firmware story's native env.

bugs.error_message: TypeError: Cannot open database because the directory does not exist - thrown by better-sqlite3's `new Database(path)` when actually running `node src/index.js` locally (not via the injected/in-memory test suite) with the default DB_PATH './data/gustik.sqlite'
bugs.root_cause: openDb() never created the parent directory of the SQLite file path. This was invisible to the whole backend test suite because every test uses dbPath=':memory:', which never touches the filesystem. Only caught by manually starting the real server and curling it (Story 1.6 smoke test) - the injected fastify tests never start a real listener against a real file path either. `backend/Dockerfile` happens to `mkdir -p data` as a build step, masking the same gap there too - a bare `npm start` outside Docker (or a Docker image without that RUN line) would hit this.
bugs.fix: openDb() now calls `fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(dbPath), { recursive: true })` before opening the database, for any non-':memory:' path. Verified via a real `node src/index.js` run against a scratch DB_PATH plus curl round-trip (GET /, GET /dashboard.js, GET /format.js, POST /readings, GET /readings/latest) - all correct, including static file MIME types.
